reviewBoundary: Two new complete junior2 15-gap four-choice cloze stories. Each contextual key and all three alternatives have a same-author explanation. Fictional model-building and family-camping incidents; no independent age or learner calibration claimed. Candidate presentation order is shuffled before the first freeze; meanings and keys are preserved.

materials.title: A railway on the table
materials.text:
For my birthday, my uncle gave me a box of model railway tracks. I wanted to use every piece, so I drew a long route across our dining table. There would be two stations, a bridge and a tunnel.

When I joined the tracks, the last piece did not ____1____ the first. A small gap remained. I tried pushing the whole railway to one side, but then the bridge hung over the ____2____ of the table.

My uncle looked at my drawing. "What do you want the train to do?" he asked.

"Travel in a complete ____3____," I said. "Then it can keep going."

"And must every piece be used?"

I looked back at the box. I had treated the number of pieces as a ____4____. Leaving some out felt like failing. But the train could not cross a gap just because I had made the route ____5____.

We removed two straight pieces and moved the far station ____6____ the bridge. Now the ends met. Before adding any buildings, I pushed a carriage around by hand to ____7____ the joins.

At the tunnel, it stopped. The tunnel entrance was too ____8____ for the tall carriage. I replaced it with a simple arch and tried again. This time the carriage passed ____9____.

Finally, I put the engine on the track. It went from one station to the other and returned without ____10____. The unused tracks lay in the box, but I no longer felt ____11____ about them.

My uncle suggested keeping the drawing. "You may have a larger space one day," he said.

I wrote the changes beside it so I would ____12____ why we had made them. The railway was smaller than my first plan, yet it did exactly what I wanted. I had learned to ____13____ my idea instead of forcing the table to fit it. Building something useful did not always mean adding ____14____. Sometimes it meant knowing what to ____15____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: The remaining gap means the final piece does not reach the first. Painting, weighing and naming do not join track ends.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: Hanging over the edge means extending beyond the table. Centre and middle are inside it, and surface does not identify its boundary.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: A complete circle allows continuous return to the start. A line, queue or row has ends and does not supply the closed route requested.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: Using all pieces had become a target in itself. Mistake, message and secret do not express that self-imposed goal.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: The narrator wanted a long route using every piece. Longer explains the pointless extra length; quietness, price and cleanliness do not solve the gap.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: Removing straight sections shortens separation, moving the station closer to the bridge. Away from lengthens it; above and outside do not describe the compact arrangement.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: Pushing a carriage by hand tests the joins before running the engine. Hiding, counting and selling do not check that the train can pass.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: A tall carriage cannot pass an entrance that is too low. Brightness and weight do not specify clearance, while wide would make passage easier.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: The new arch allows the carriage through. Upstairs is not part of the route, backwards changes direction rather than clearance, and nearby does not mean entering and exiting.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: The completed route lets the engine return without stopping at a gap or obstruction. Learning, sleeping and shouting do not describe the model train.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: The narrator no longer feels bad about unused pieces. Excited would remove a positive feeling, certain concerns belief and thirsty has no relevance.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: Recording reasons preserves them to remember later. Guess and deny contradict a written explanation; change the reasons is not the purpose.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: The narrator adapts the plan to the real table. Forgetting abandons it, protecting resists changes, and repeating does not explain the successful revision.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: The conclusion contrasts adding more with removing needless pieces. Noise, paint and weight were not the overbuilding problem.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: Leave out summarises deliberately unused tracks. Look after means care for, wait for delay and pay back repay, none describes omission.

materials.title: The noise outside the tent
materials.text:
My brother and I were sleeping in a tent in our grandparents' garden. In daylight, the place was ____1____: we played there every holiday. After dark, even the apple tree looked different.

We switched off the torch. Soon I heard a scraping ____2____ near the tent door and held my breath.

"Did you hear that?" I whispered.

My brother nodded. He was usually the ____3____ one, first to climb trees or enter dark rooms. Now he pulled his sleeping bag closer.

I imagined a large animal approaching. But the garden gate was ____4____, and the dog was asleep indoors. What could it be?

"Let's look," my brother said. His torch beam pointed straight at his pillow: his hands were ____5____.

We laughed, which made it easier to ____6____. I opened the door slightly. A bright patch lay on the grass. It was not an animal, just the ____7____ from Grandpa's kitchen.

Grandpa stood outside, collecting our empty cups in a metal bowl. The bowl scraped a chair as he bent down.

"I didn't mean to ____8____ you," he said.

After helping him, we returned to the tent. The garden felt ____9____ again because we understood the noise.

We placed the torch where we could both ____10____ it. We also agreed that asking an adult was better than inventing the biggest possible ____11____.

In the morning, Grandma asked if we had been brave. "We were ____12____," my brother replied, "but we looked, and then we understood."

I liked that. Bravery did not have to mean feeling no ____13____. It could mean taking a small step to discover what was ____14____, with help nearby.

We slept outside again the next night, waiting for Grandpa to finish first. He collected the cups ____15____ we turned off the torch.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: Repeated holiday play makes the garden familiar. Empty is not established, dangerous contradicts the known safe setting and new contradicts previous visits.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: Heard and scraping require sound. Colour, smell and taste use different senses.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: First to climb or enter dark rooms characterises the normally brave brother. Quiet, young and careless are not the quality contrasted with this fear.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: A closed gate helps explain doubt about a large animal entering. Broken and missing would allow entry, and painted does not restrict access.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: Nervous shaking explains aiming the torch badly. Dry, clean and free do not account for that fearful loss of control.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: Shared laughter reduces fear and makes acting and opening the door easier. Complaining and hiding do not lead to investigation, and dreaming contradicts their awake actions.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: The bright shape comes from the kitchen light. Smoke is not a bright shape here, music is not visible, and rain has no stated kitchen source.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: Grandpa apologises for frightening the children unintentionally. He is not inviting, following or teaching them in this line.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: Knowing the ordinary source makes the familiar garden ordinary again. Size, temperature and distance have not changed.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: They place the torch within reach for use. Throwing or breaking it is not the preparation needed, and losing it defeats the purpose.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: The feared large animal had grown into an imagined monster. Meal, garden and bowl do not name the frightening invented explanation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: He acknowledges fear while describing looking and understanding. Anger and hunger are not the episode, and asleep contradicts their investigation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: The lesson is that bravery can include fear. Interest, pain and pride are not the feeling explicitly explored in this night-time scare.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: Finding what is happening replaces imagined explanations with observation. Beauty, price and missing objects do not describe the unknown noise event.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: Collecting cups before lights-out avoids repeating the scare. Unless gives the wrong condition, although an unsupported concession and while simultaneous action rather than the preventive sequence.
